utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The next witness to be called, Mr. Gaynor, is a protected witness. He would be examined in closed session?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, the next witness to be called, I was informed that you'd like to seek protective measures for the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. I should also advise the Court that we are prepared to proceed with that witness tomorrow morning at 9.00 a.m., as it has been scheduled but not today. We can advise the Court in the interim, if the Court permits, of the protective measures, the specific protective measures involved, if there's any question about those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it that the protective measures you would like to discuss them in private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, although I would have to break to find out if there's been any modification of the proposed protective measures in any respect and to ensure that the measures we're proposing to the Chamber are accurate in all respects.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course witness protection is to some extent a public matter and to some extent it's not. It's a public matter to the extent that the public should be informed about the reasons. The Chamber has been informed -- Mr. Stewart, and I take it that you're aware of the reasons why the Prosecution seeks protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, yes, Your Honour, I had a discussion and then Mr. Harmon as a result of that discussion sent me a memo of the e-mail of the main points. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It has not been formally been filed. An oral application could perhaps be made in such a way that the Chamber could give its decision on the basis of that oral request and to what extent that should be done in private session, I leave that to you, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm grateful for that opportunity. As mentioned, I would appreciate the opportunity to break briefly for the reasons I mentioned and -- before I make application orally to move into private session, if necessary, and identify the basis for the application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber might even deliver a decision right away after that because we were informed about the reasons and we were also informed that there was no objection from the Defence. So the Chamber has already --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- formed an opinion, but nevertheless for -- to have everything on the record, we would like the request to be made orally. And after that short break then, the Chamber would also like to give a decision in relation to a videolink requested by the Prosecution. We'll then -- how much time would you need, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm sure no more than 10 minutes is necessary, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll then adjourn for 10 minutes. --- Break taken at 11.50 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If we could move into private session at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are back in open session. The Chamber will now deliver its decision on the Prosecution's application, which was made in court this morning, and which was not opposed by the Defence, for the evidence of Witness 680 to be heard in closed session. And I add to it, with pseudonym. As the Chamber has said on numerous occasions, the party seeking protective measures for a witness must show that such measures are justified by demonstrating the existence of an objectively grounded risk to the security or welfare of the witness (or the witness's family), should it become known that the witness gave evidence before the Tribunal. It will usually be sufficient if it is shown that a threat was made against the witness or the witness's family. In addition, the Chamber must be satisfied that protective measures less restrictive than those sought would not address the security concerns of the witness. In the present instance, the Prosecution observed that given the position formerly held by the witness, the nature of his testimony, in particular the fact that it may implicate high-level Bosnian Serbs, will likely antagonise persons residing in the former Yugoslavia, to a security risk. Furthermore, the Prosecution submitted that lesser protective measures than closed session and pseudonym would be inadequate in the case of Witness 680 because his testimony is so unique that it would, of itself, reveal his identity. In light of these arguments, the Chamber considers that the requirements for the requested protective measures have been met and orders that Witness 680 testify in closed session and under pseudonym. This concludes the Chamber's decision. I would also like to deliver a decision pursuant to Rule 71 of the Rules. This decision addresses a Prosecution motion dated the 16th of June, of this year, in which the Prosecutor requests that Witness 031 be heard via videoconference link. The reasons for this request are described in the motion and relate to the personal circumstances of the witness. Rule 71 bis states that, and I quote: "[A] Trial Chamber may, in the interests of justice, order that testimony be received via videoconference link." In the present case, the Chamber considers that the personal circumstances of the witness, as indicated by the Prosecution, provide strong grounds for the witness to be allowed to give testimony via videoconference link. The Chamber notes that the Defence does not object to such a course of action in respect of Witness 031. Furthermore, on numerous occasions, including in this Chamber's decision of the 4th of October, 2004, and in the decision of the 28th of May, 1997, in Delalic, and others, this Tribunal has found that a party suffers no material disadvantage by examining a witness via videolink. In light of these considerations, the Chamber finds that it is in the interests of justice that Witness 031 be heard via videoconference link. This concludes the decision pursuant to Rule 71 bis in relation to Witness 031. Is there any other procedural issue to be raised?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, not from our side.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Nor from the Defence side, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'd like to make two observations. First, although the next witness has been scheduled for tomorrow, if we go quicker than expected, of course, it's always a pity if we can't use the time, and the Prosecutor certainly is well aware of the fact that 22nd of July is 22nd of July. So therefore, to the extent possible, it is of no use I think at this moment to start a long debate on whether we could have done it another way, but the Prosecutor is just reminded to use the time as efficient as possible. Another matter which I would just like to briefly mention is about your cross-examination, Mr. Krajisnik. In many of the questions you have put today to the witness, one could wonder what made you believe that the witness would have had knowledge about it, apart from perhaps from a few questions. You should be aware that if you ask the question whether he knows that and then there follows a line, and if the witness says, No, I don't know that, that we have at that moment nothing in evidence. That should be perfectly clear to you and I think it's also perhaps wise to consider why a certain witness -- why you would expect that he has knowledge of certain matters, and perhaps the best way to find out is to ask him first whether he has any knowledge of certain events and not just to ask the witness whether he knows that. Because if you ask a witness whether he knows that a person was born near Zvornik or wherever, that does not establish that that person was born there. As a matter of fact, we know nothing more than we did before. This is just a general observation the Chamber would like to make in respect of the way you have put additional questions to witnesses in cross-examination. We'll adjourn until tomorrow morning, and I announce to the parties that arrangements have been made that if on Thursday morning we would find that we are not able to finish the next witness by Friday, that we'll have some additional time. Mr. Stewart, we gained some time today. I hope that we will not ask for more time on Thursday.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I ask something about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: About the timetabling, if we are at the possible on, say, Thursday at quarter to 2.00 or it becomes apparent as we approach that time on Thursday that the use of the afternoon session for which provisional arrangements could be made would enable us to finish the witness on Thursday, then I'm sure Your Honour can see, certainly on our side, it may be true to the Prosecution, it may be true for the Trial Chamber, but -- it would be more helpful then, assuming that there isn't a problem of readiness, but it would be more helpful to use that provisionally arranged session and finish the witness than for everyone to come back on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that would certainly be something we could consider as a matter of fact, not to say we need only two hours more, so let's wait until tomorrow. We'll certainly then -- upon an application we'll consider then to finish the witness on that same Thursday.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 22nd day of June, 2005, at 9.00 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.24 p.m.,
